message.content: {"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The model states the correct AJCC size rules but still assigns T1, indicating it did not use the actual tumor size (3.5 cm). {"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (6.5 cm) but then stated that T2 covers tumors 2–5 cm and concluded 6.5 cm → T2. This reveals an explicit, wrong AJCC rule in its reasoning, so the failure is due to incorrect staging knowledge, not extraction or arithmetic."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states a tumor size of 5.2 cm (>5 cm → T3). The model concluded T2, which would only be correct for a tumor ≤5 cm, implying it either overlooked or mis-read the 5.2 cm measurement and instead used ≤5 cm data (e.g., the 5.0 cm firmness note). The AJCC rule it quoted is correct; it simply failed to use the correct size from the text."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states the largest invasive tumor measures only 1.2 cm, with each visible mass about 1 cm. The model nevertheless classified the case as T2 (>2 cm), which implies it mis-read another measurement (e.g., the 4–4.5 cm distances between masses or to margins) as the tumor size. Thus the error stems from extracting the wrong size data, not from misuse of staging rules once the correct size is known."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (2.0 cm) but then stated that this value meets the T2 criterion of “> 2.0 cm,” mistakenly treating 2.0 cm as greater than 2.0 cm. The AJCC rule itself was cited correctly (T2 is >2 cm), so the fault lies in the numeric comparison, not in AJCC knowledge."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size as 9 cm and even restated the AJCC rule that tumors \"more than 5 cm\" are T3, but it still concluded T2. The facts and staging rule were present; the error came from an illogical numerical comparison (treating 9 cm as ≤5 cm)."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states “Greatest dimension (pT) : 4.2 cm (pT2).” The model nevertheless says “The tumor size is 2 cm or less,” showing it failed to capture the correct 4.2 cm measurement from the text. The staging rule itself (≤2 cm → T1) is correct; the problem is that the model extracted the wrong tumor size, not that it applied the rule incorrectly."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (55 mm) but compared it incorrectly, treating 55 mm as \u0003≤5 cm. This numeric conversion error led it to label the tumor T2 instead of the correct T3."}

{"error_cause":"Conflicting Ground Truth","reason":"The report states a tumor size of 3.4 cm without chest-wall or skin invasion. AJCC 7th: >2 cm ≤5 cm → T2, >5 cm → T3. So the model’s T2 matches AJCC, while the dataset label T3 contradicts the report’s facts and staging rules."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted the 2.2 cm tumor size and even wrote in its rationale that this corresponds to T2 per AJCC rules, yet the value it ultimately output was “3,” not T2. The facts were recognized; the model simply produced the wrong final classification, so the mistake lies in its inference/output step, not in information extraction or staging rules."}

This is a faulty numeric comparison, not a knowledge or extraction issue."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted the fact that the report explicitly states \"T Stage: 2,\" but it chose to disregard this information and declared the stage \"indeterminate\" because tumor size was not listed. Thus, it had the necessary fact yet drew the wrong conclusion, making this an inference error rather than an extraction or knowledge error."}
